sections.h2: What kind of place is Arlington Heights for a home seller?
sections.html:
Arlington Heights is a village in Cook County, about 25 miles northwest of downtown Chicago, with a small portion reaching into Lake County. It covers 16.61 square miles of land, nearly all of it built up, so a house sale here competes with other established neighborhoods rather than open lots.

The 2020 census counted 77,676 people, which made it the 15th most populous municipality in Illinois. The Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate is 76,216, a drop of 1.9% from the 2020 base. Roughly one in five residents is 65 or older, and the median age in 2020 was 43.0.

sections.h2: How did Arlington Heights grow, and why does that matter for an older house?
sections.html:
The settlement began as a stop on the railroad, first called Dunton, and took the name Arlington Heights in 1874. Farms and greenhouses dominated the land until after World War II.

The big change came in the 1950s and 1960s. Car ownership, the baby boom and annexations pushed the population to 64,884 by 1970, and nearly all the available land was built on by then. If you own a house from that period, expect a buyer's inspector to look hard at the original roof framing, the electrical panel, galvanized or older copper supply lines and the basement walls.

  • Pull your permit history before listing, because open or unfinalized permits slow a closing.
  • Keep receipts for the furnace, water heater and roof, since buyers ask for ages.
  • Check whether a finished basement, deck or addition was permitted at the time it was built.

sections.h2: What is going on with the Arlington Park property?
sections.html:
The former racetrack at 3200 W. Euclid Ave. is a 326-acre site that the Chicago Bears Football Club bought in February 2023. The village runs a dedicated redevelopment page for it, and that page now carries a statement that the team announced it would focus on a stadium opportunity in Indiana.

The same page says the village still sees the property as a highly viable redevelopment site because of its size, transportation access and location in the northwest suburbs. For a seller nearby, the practical point is that the future use of that land is unsettled. Buyers will ask what you know about it, so read the current village page and answer from what it says instead of guessing.

sections.h2: Which school districts serve Arlington Heights homes?
sections.html:
Most of the village sits in Arlington Heights School District 25 for elementary and middle grades and in Township High School District 214 for high school. Several other districts reach into the edges of the village, so the address on the contract decides which schools a buyer gets.

  • District 25 serves most elementary and middle school students, including South Middle School and Thomas Middle School.
  • Prospect Heights District 23, Wheeling District 21, Community Consolidated Districts 59 and 15, and District 57 cover portions of the village.
  • John Hersey High School is the one public high school inside the village; Buffalo Grove, Prospect, Rolling Meadows and Wheeling also take students from parts of it.
  • A small area feeds Palatine High School in District 211.

Look up the school assignment for your exact street before you write a listing description or answer a buyer's question.

sections.h2: Can a buyer use the house as a short-term rental in Arlington Heights?
sections.html:
No. The Village Board passed an ordinance on March 2, 2026 that requires a minimum 30-day consecutive stay for every residential rental property, and it took effect July 1, 2026. Existing short-term rentals were not grandfathered, and bookings shorter than 30 days are treated as nuisances.

Hotels, motels and lodging rooms are exempt. The village also wrote in an exception for sellers: a buyer and seller can sign an agreement that lets the seller stay on for fewer than 30 consecutive days, provided the rental agreement is executed together with the contract to sell. If you need a few weeks after closing to move, put that agreement in writing at the same time as the sale contract.

sections.h2: What do permits and building codes mean when you sell?
sections.html:
The Building and Life Safety Department handles permits, and applications and inspection scheduling run through the village's Civic Access Portal. The office is open 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday through Friday, opening at 9:30 a.m. on the first and third Wednesday of each month, and its number is 847-368-5560.

Construction hours in the village are 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. on weekdays and 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. on weekends, which matters if you plan repairs before closing. The village has also adopted 2024 editions of the International codes, replacing the 2018 base codes, with an effective date of January 1, 2027. Applicants are told to review the updated requirements before they submit permit applications.

sections.h2: How are the deed and transfer tax handled on an Arlington Heights sale?
sections.html:
The county recorder collects the state real estate transfer tax by selling revenue stamps, as described by the Illinois Department of Revenue. The buyer and seller fill out Form PTAX-203, the Illinois Real Estate Transfer Declaration, and file it in the county where the property sits.

Counties may add a tax of 25 cents per $500 of value, and home rule municipalities may impose their own transfer tax on top. Ask the title company which taxes apply to your parcel and which party pays each one.

For recording in Cook County, the County Clerk's fee schedule lists $107 for a deed under its Document Class 1, a figure that includes the county recording fee, a GIS fee, a document storage fee, the state rental housing support fee and a non-government filer fee. That schedule took effect April 1, 2024. Parcels in the Lake County portion are recorded with that county instead, so confirm which county holds your parcel number.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale make sense for an Arlington Heights house?
sections.html:
A direct cash purchase fits when the house needs work, when an estate or divorce has to be settled, or when you cannot wait through months of showings and a buyer's loan approval. You trade some of the price a fully renovated listing might reach for speed and certainty.

  • Compare any offer against what a listing would net after agent fees, repairs and carrying costs.
  • Ask whether the buyer pays for the title search and recording, and get the answer in the contract.
  • Confirm the closing date and what happens to your belongings and utilities on that day.

Whichever route you choose, a signed purchase agreement, a title commitment and a clear closing statement are what protect you.

faqs.q: How long does it take to sell a house in Arlington Heights for cash?
faqs.a: A cash sale can close on the date written into the contract, since no lender approval is involved. The deed still has to be recorded with the correct county, and Cook County recording is done through the County Clerk. Set the closing date in the contract and confirm it with the title company.

faqs.q: Do I need to fix my house before selling in Arlington Heights?
faqs.a: No, but open permits and code problems are worth sorting out first. Pull your permit record from the Building and Life Safety Department, and finalize anything unfinished. Cosmetic repairs are optional if you sell as-is.

faqs.q: Can I rent my house after closing if I need more time?
faqs.a: Yes. The village allows a buyer and seller to sign a rental agreement shorter than 30 consecutive days, as long as it is executed in conjunction with the contract to sell. Without that agreement, stays under 30 days at a residential rental are treated as nuisances under the village ordinance.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax on an Arlington Heights sale?
faqs.a: The contract decides, so read it before you sign. The state tax is collected as revenue stamps through the county recorder, counties may add 25 cents per $500, and home rule municipalities may add their own. Your title company can list each tax and who is responsible.

The county where the parcel sits. Most of Arlington Heights is in Cook County, where the County Clerk records deeds, and a portion lies in Lake County. Check your parcel number to confirm before closing day.
